title: Org admin policy layer: configurable compliance toggles for network, sharing, and exports
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Add a new policy layer in the Org Admin surface that exposes three atomic compliance toggles: IP allowlisting enforcement, disable-public-sharing (prevent links/shared snippets), and strict data-export controls (disable CSV/JSON export + block copy from console). These toggles must be enforceable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and integrate with RBAC v2 and SSO/SAML identity attributes (org/group claims). Must emit structured audit events and honor existing retention policies in Audit Logging subsystem.
acceptance_criteria: Admin console presents three independent toggles with explanatory copy and link to policy docs
Toggles are available via Admin REST API and SDK with same semantics as console
RBAC v2 evaluation layer enforces the toggles for roles without privileged flags
SSO/SAML group claims can be mapped to exempt roles (allowlist) and settings are scoped to org and team levels

Audit logs record change events and enforcement incidents with consistent event schema and include actor, timestamp, policy key, previous value, source (API/console/automation), and affected resources
E2E tests validate that when export control is enabled: UI export buttons are disabled, export API returns 403, and attempts to copy raw content via bulk endpoints are blocked
IP allowlist enforcement prevents new connections from disallowed CIDR ranges for console/API and surfaces clear 403 with guidance
No regression to existing telemetry or latency SLOs beyond acceptable threshold (apdex drop < 2%)
Feature flag gate exists to roll out as beta to pilots before org-wide release
notes: This ticket is the implementation epic for the Admin Controls compliance suite. We will implement enforcement at three layers: API gateway (network-level), platform policy enforcer (RBAC v2 extension), and UI/console affordances. Audit logging will reuse the structured schema from the audit project and add two new event types: policy.toggle_change and policy.enforcement_block.
updates: 2025-02-18: Drafted scope and acceptance criteria. Assigned to Ethan. Identified dependency on RBAC v2 feature toggles and audit-logs schema change (ENG-35167).
2025-02-21: Design sync with PM and Design completed — UX copy for toggles approved (Marisol Gomez). Console mockups in drive: https://drive.redwood.example.com/admin-compliance-toggle-mockups

2025-02-25: Security review kickoff. Preliminary threat model: risk of bypass via legacy API keys; mitigation: enforce check in token middleware and add CI test. Added dependency on SSO/SAML claim mapping EPIC.

2025-02-28: Implementation plan agreed: phase 1 (console + API flags + audit events), phase 2 (gateway IP enforcement + private deploy installer changes), phase 3 (pilot, collect logs, SLA verification).
2025-03-02: First PR opened for policy store and admin API: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1489 — initial schema and controller. Added unit tests for toggle persistence.
tech_decisions: Enforce IP allowlist at gateway (layer 3/4) for requests originating outside private deployments; also add policy enforcer hook in platform middleware for Console/API checks
Represent toggles as first-class Policy objects in the policy store with versioned schema to support rollbacks
Use SAML/SSO group claim mapping with explicit deny-exempt lists rather than freeform allow rules to reduce accidental exposure
Audit events will use event_type field and follow existing newline-delimited JSON schema to ease ingestion into observability pipelines
suggested_rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind beta-admin for 2 pilot orgs; 2) Collect enforcement metrics and audit events for 2 weeks; 3) Iterate on UX copy and error guidance; 4) Gradual 25/50/100% rollout with monitoring dashboards (export denial rate, false positives, error rates); 5) Announce to customers and update docs.
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy store CRUD + migration tests
Integration tests: console toggles persist and map to API responses
E2E: simulate SSO group mappings to ensure exempted roles bypass enforcement
Pen test: attempt bypass using legacy API keys and verify blocked
Load test: ensure policy checks add <5ms median overhead to token validation path
qa_notes: Coordinate with Solutions Engineering to enroll two pilot customers with Dedicated and Private deployments. Ensure audit retention aligns with compliance package (90/365 days depending on customer contract).
